newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec S&P 500s end up on window dressing, bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec S&P 500s end up on window dressing, bonds.

text.p: U.S. December Standard and Poor's 500 futures ended strongly higher, buoyed by a late Treasury bond rally and by aggressive buying from major firms.
Traders said they suspected fiscal year-end window dressing from mutual funds was behind the heavy buying from Wall Street firms.
"Basically it was a day of no minor players," one S&P 500 futures trader said. "The big funds dominated the market," he said.
December S&Ps rallied to a high of 710.50 in afternoon trading after triggering buy stops at 706.25 and 707.00.
A late Treasury bond rally powered by declining commodity prices generated further buying interest in S&Ps, traders said.
Some traders said S&Ps technically looked poised for more gains early on Friday.
"It's a technical buy," one trader said.
But one broker said the market may have gone too far ahead of key employment data due on Friday.
"This could be a Humpty Dumpty scenario where they've been set up for a good fall," the trader said.
Traders, on average, were looking for U.S. October nonfarm payrolls to rise 212,000, and the unemployment rate to hold steady at 5.2 percent from September.
Traders said locals were mostly sellers on the day. Traders said smaller players were wary heading into the critical data Friday.
Traders pegged resistance in December S&Ps at 711.00 and 712.00 for early on Friday.
Preliminary support was expected at 708.50, which had been resistance on Thursday, they said.
Strong technology stocks fueled strength in Nasdaq futures, rounding out the bullish stock index picture, traders said. December Nasdaq 100 futures finished up 17.75 points to 759.85.

At settlement, December S&Ps were up 6.85 points at 709.65, New Composites were up 2.85 at 376.60, Value Lines were up 5.30 at 647.80, Nikkeis fell 50.0 points to 20,570 and Midcap 400s were up 1.55 at 244.05. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
